Voting Locations

Vote in the Upcoming Election

In the November 3, 2026 General Election, voters will cast their ballots for federal, state, and local candidates, as well as state ballot questions and local ballot questions.

See the links on the left to find 24-hour Drop Box and Voter Service and Polling Center (VSPC) locations, use our "Find My Nearest" tool for the most convenient place to vote or drop off your ballot, make a Curbside Ballot Pickup reservation, and check VSPC wait times.

NEED VOTING ASSISTANCE?

Visit a Voter Service and Polling Center between October 19, 2026 - November 3, 2026 to register to vote, update your registration, request a replacement mail ballot, vote with assistance or assistive devices, or vote on a ballot marking device. Click here to see the hours of operation for each VSPC.

Accessibility: Voters with a disability

Every VSPC is HAVA/ADA accessible and offers several accessible voting interfaces that allow voters with various disabilities to effectively vote, review their choices, and cast a paper ballot in a private and independent manner. Voters may request any of the following: 

  • Wheelchair-accessible voting booth
  • Audio ballot and headphones
  • Large font size and/or high contrast on ballot marking devices
  • Ability to connect to a voter's sip and puff device or paddles

Election Judges are also available to assist voters upon request. 


STEPS TO VOTE

Update Voter Registration



Ballots will be mailed starting September 18, 2026, for voters in the military and voters living overseas and on October 2, 2026, for all other voters.

Visit www.GoVoteColorado.gov to check that your voter registration is active and your mailing address is current. 

Ballots are not forwarded even if you have submitted a Change of Address Form to the post office. 

Register/Update

Watch Your Mailbox



Ballots will be mailed to active registered voters starting October 2, 2026. Please allow one full week for your ballot to arrive. 

If you do not receive your mail ballot, please go online at www.GoVoteColorado.gov and verify your voter registration address is correct. Update your address if necessary and a replacement ballot will be mailed to your new address.

Ballots cannot be forwarded by the Postal Service.

All other issues, please contact our office at 303-795-4511.

After October 26, 2026, we can no longer send ballots by mail. Instead, you must to go to a Voter Service and Polling Center to update your registration and request a ballot.

Return Voted Ballot


Read all instructions with your ballot. Mark your choices by filling in the ovals with a black or blue pen.  Be sure to sign the return envelope.

Return your ballot to any one of our 24 hour ballot box locations or by mail with paid postage. Ballots must be received by Arapahoe County by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day to be counted. Postmarks do not count as received.
Track Your Ballot



Track your ballot online with BallotTrax. You also can sign up for free text, phone or email messages when your ballot has been mailed to you and received by Arapahoe County.
